title: LLM Knowledge Bases - using LLMs to build and maintain personal knowledge wikis
description: Andrej Karpathy described his workflow for using LLMs to build personal knowledge bases: ingesting source documents into a raw/ directory, using LLMs to incrementally 'compile' a wiki of .md files with summaries, backlinks, and categorized concepts. He uses Obsidian as the IDE frontend. Once the wiki is large enough (~100 articles, ~400K words), he can ask LLM agents complex questions against it. The LLM maintains all wiki data, with features like auto-maintaining index files, 'health checks' for data integrity, linting for inconsistencies, and synthetic data generation for potential finetuning.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: OpenAI's existential questions
description: TechCrunch coverage examining OpenAI's strategic direction and challenges as the company navigates the evolving AI landscape.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration seems to be thawing
description: Analysis of Anthropic's improving relationship with the Trump administration, following previous tensions between the AI company and government officials.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Anthropic launches Claude Design, a new product for creating quick visuals
description: Anthropic has introduced Claude Design, a new product focused on visual content creation, expanding the Claude ecosystem beyond text.
author: Aisha Malik

title: Sources: Cursor in talks to raise $2B+ at $50B valuation as enterprise growth surges
description: AI code editor Cursor is reportedly in discussions to raise over $2 billion at a $50 billion valuation, driven by strong enterprise adoption growth.
author: Marina Temkin

title: 'Tokenmaxxing' is making developers less productive than they think
description: Article exploring the phenomenon of 'tokenmaxxing' - excessive use of AI tokens - and how it may be negatively impacting developer productivity rather than improving it.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Kevin Weil and Bill Peebles exit OpenAI as company continues to shed 'side quests'
description: Two more high-profile executives depart OpenAI as the company refocuses on core initiatives and moves away from what internal sources describe as 'side quests'.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on my laptop drew me a better pelican than Claude Opus 4.7
description: Simon Willison compared the pelican-riding-a-bicycle benchmark results from two major model releases: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from Alibaba and Claude Opus 4.7 from Anthropic. He found that the local Qwen model produced a better pelican than Anthropic's latest Opus model, highlighting the competitive landscape of open-weight vs proprietary models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release of llm-anthropic 0.25 with Claude Opus 4.7 support
description: New release of the llm-anthropic plugin adding support for Claude Opus 4.7, which includes the new 'thinking_effort': 'xhigh' parameter, new thinking_display and thinking_adaptive boolean options, and increased default max_tokens to the maximum allowed for each model.
author: Simon Willison

title: datasette.io news preview tool built with Claude Artifacts
description: Simon used Claude.ai and Claude Artifacts to build a custom preview UI for datasette.io's news.yaml file. The tool allows pasting YAML to preview rendering and highlights markdown or YAML errors. Demonstrates Claude's ability to clone GitHub repos and build tools interactively.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI takes aim at Anthropic with beefed-up Codex that gives it more power over your desktop
description: OpenAI has enhanced its Codex model to provide more desktop control capabilities, positioning it as a competitor to Anthropic's offerings in the AI coding space.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Factory hits $1.5B valuation to build AI coding for enterprises
description: AI coding startup Factory has reached a $1.5 billion valuation, focusing on enterprise AI coding solutions as demand for AI development tools continues to grow.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Canva's AI assistant can now call various tools to make designs for you
description: Canva has enhanced its AI assistant with tool-calling capabilities, allowing it to create designs by invoking various tools and services.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Google now lets you explore the web side-by-side with AI Mode
description: Google has introduced AI Mode, a new browsing feature that allows users to explore the web with AI assistance side-by-side with traditional browsing.
author: Aisha Malik

title: Roblox's AI assistant gets new agentic tools to plan, build, and test games
description: Roblox has enhanced its AI assistant with new agentic capabilities that can help plan, build, and test games within the Roblox platform.
author: Aisha Malik

title: InsightFinder raises $15M to help companies figure out where AI agents go wrong
description: InsightFinder has raised $15 million in funding for its platform that helps companies identify and diagnose issues with AI agent behavior.
author: Ram Iyer

title: This simulation startup wants to be the Cursor for physical AI
description: Profile of Antioch, a simulation startup that aims to provide development tools for physical AI systems, positioning itself similarly to how Cursor serves software development.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Replit Agent 4 - AI for creative collaboration between humans and agents
description: Amjad Masad introduced Replit Agent 4, described as 'The first AI built for creative collaboration between humans and agents' featuring an infinite canvas design interface. Replit continues to focus on autonomous agents that can 'write code and deploy apps from text prompts,' fully integrated into their development platform.
author: Amjad Masad

title: ICLR 2026: 1,200 papers with public code or data
description: Reddit discussion highlighting that ICLR 2026 conference (starting April 22nd in Rio de Janeiro) features 1,200 accepted papers with associated public code, data, or demo links. The conference represents cutting-edge AI research with open-source reproducibility.
author: r/MachineLearning Community

title: Datasette 1.0a27: CSRF protection replaced with Sec-Fetch-Site headers
description: Major Datasette alpha release replacing Django-style CSRF tokens with modern browser headers based on Filippo Valsorda's research. Also introduces new RenameTableEvent for plugins reacting to table renames during SQL transactions.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google releases Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS with prompt-directed audio generation
description: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a text-to-speech model that can be directed using elaborate prompts. Simon built a UI tool to try it out and found the prompting guide surprisingly detailed, requiring extensive scene descriptions and director's notes to generate short audio clips.
author: Simon Willison

title: Has industry effectively killed off academic machine learning research in 2026?
description: Reddit discussion on r/MachineLearning about the relationship between industry and academia in ML research, exploring whether industry dominance is crowding out academic research or creating new collaboration opportunities.
author: r/MachineLearning Community

title: OpenAI announces GPT-5.4-Cyber and Trusted Access for Cyber program
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.4-Cyber, a cyber-permissive variant fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity use cases. They also extended their Trusted Access for Cyber program where users can verify identity via government ID to gain reduced friction access to OpenAI's models for security work.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cybersecurity looks like proof of work now - economic incentives in AI security
description: Analysis of UK's AI Safety Institute report on Claude Mythos showing that the more tokens (money) spent on security reviews, the better results. This creates an economic incentive to spend more tokens on defense than attackers spend on exploitation, and makes open source libraries more valuable as security investment can be shared across users.
author: Simon Willison (citing Drew Breunig)

title: Steve Yegge vs Google on AI adoption - industry-wide 20/60/20 split
description: Steve Yegge claimed Google has poor AI adoption (similar to John Deere), with 20% agentic power users, 20% refusers, 60% using basic tools. Google's Addy Osmani and Demis Hassabis pushed back, stating over 40K SWEs use agentic coding weekly with access to custom models, skills, and orchestrators.
author: Simon Willison (curating Steve Yegge, Addy Osmani, Demis Hassabis)

title: Exploring the new servo crate - embeddable browser engine for Rust
description: Simon investigated the April 2026 release of servo v0.1.0 crate, an embeddable browser engine for Rust. He used Claude Code to build a servo-shot CLI tool for taking screenshots and explored whether it could compile to WebAssembly (not feasible due to heavy threading and SpiderMonkey dependencies).
author: Simon Willison

title: Bryan Cantrill on LLMs and the virtue of laziness
description: Bryan Cantrill argues that LLMs lack the virtue of laziness - work costs nothing to them, so they dump more onto systems rather than optimizing. Human laziness forces us to develop crisp abstractions because we don't want to waste our time on clunky ones. LLMs will make systems larger, not better, appealing to vanity metrics.
author: Simon Willison (citing Bryan Cantrill)
